# Library Lending: operations guide

Version 0.1.0 of the specification: 2 monitors, 1 job, 2 dependencies and 20 endpoints. For the people who run the live system: where it runs, what to look at each day, what to do when a monitor's objective is missed, what runs on its own, what it depends on, and how its data is saved and brought back.

## 1. Where it runs

| Environment | Purpose | Run by | Promotes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| development | A developer's machine, with a throwaway database. | vendor | staging |
| staging | A copy of production the librarians try a release on before it goes live. | vendor | production |
| production | The live system at the desk, on the library's own hosts. | customer |   |

**Insight on production:** The library's board keeps member data on hosts it controls, so its IT staff build each release from the source and run production themselves; the vendor runs development and staging.

## 2. Daily checklist

What to look at on the live system each day. Tick the last column as each is seen to be as expected.

| Check | What to look at | Expected | Seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monitor catalogue-latency (production) | How long listBooks takes to answer at the desk. | Nine calls in ten answer within 200 milliseconds over each opening day. |   |
| Monitor overdue-notices-sent (production) | Whether the nightly job published LoanOverdue for every loan that became overdue. | Every loan marked overdue in a night has its LoanOverdue message published the same night. |   |
| Job markOverdue | Its last run, on the schedule `0 2 * * *` (UTC). | It ran, and no item is kept apart after its last try; the section Jobs says where a kept item is. |   |
| Dependency eventBus | That it answers over amqp. | It answers within PT1S. |   |
| Dependency feeLedger | That it answers over https. | It answers within PT5S. |   |

## 3. Monitors

### catalogue-latency

How long listBooks takes to answer at the desk. In production. Objective: Nine calls in ten answer within 200 milliseconds over each opening day.

Verifies LIB-7.

**Insight:** A slow catalogue is the first thing a librarian notices, and the commissioning check measured it only once.

Watched in production (Library Lending in Go and PostgreSQL) with Prometheus: The service's request histogram for listBooks. Alert: the desk's on-call channel.

When the objective is missed:

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Find the slow query | Open the database's slow query log for the hour the objective was missed. | The slowest statement and its plan are named. |
| 2. Rebuild the search index | If the slow statement is the catalogue search, rebuild the index on title and author after closing. | The catalogue answers within 200 milliseconds again on the next opening day. |

### overdue-notices-sent

Whether the nightly job published LoanOverdue for every loan that became overdue. In production. Objective: Every loan marked overdue in a night has its LoanOverdue message published the same night.

Verifies LIB-4.

Watched in production (Library Lending in Go and PostgreSQL) with Prometheus: The count of loans marked overdue against the count of LoanOverdue messages published, per night. Alert: the desk's on-call channel.

The specification does not say what to do when the objective is missed; the steps are written under the monitor's response.

## 4. Jobs

What the system runs on its own. A job acts as its role and may do only what the role's permissions allow.

| Job | Starts | Acts as | After a failure | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| markOverdue | on the schedule `0 2 * * *` (UTC) | scheduler | tried again up to 3 times, then kept apart for the librarian role | Every night, finds the open loans past their due date, marks each overdue, and publishes LoanOverdue for it, so the member is told. |

**Insight on markOverdue:** Overnight, when no one is at the desk, so a loan is overdue from the first morning after its due date.

### markOverdue: an item kept apart

A loan the job could not mark on any try is kept apart, with the error of its last try, on the list of loans the job could not mark. The member is not told about the loan until it leaves the list.

Handled by the librarian role: a person who holds it looks at each kept item, then tries it again or discards it.

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Look at it | Open the list of loans the job could not mark, and read the error of the loan's last try. | Why the loan was not marked is known. |
| 2. Try it again | If the error is gone, such as the event bus answering again, try the loan again from the list. | The loan is marked overdue, its LoanOverdue is published, and it leaves the list. |
| 3. Discard it | If the loan should not be overdue, such as one returned before its due date and recorded late, discard it from the list. | The list no longer holds it, and the loan is as it was. |

## 5. Channels

Each message, what carries it and who publishes and consumes it. A channel no dependency carries is the system's own.

| Channel | Carried by | Message | Published by | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fee.waivers | the system itself | FeeWaiverDecided | workflow fee-waiver |   |
| loan.lifecycle | eventBus | LoanCreated | operation createLoan |   |
| loan.lifecycle | eventBus | LoanReturned | operation returnLoan |   |
| loan.lifecycle | eventBus | LoanLost | operation reportLost |   |
| loan.overdue | eventBus | LoanOverdue | job markOverdue |   |

## 6. Dependencies

What fails or waits when a dependency is down: every operation, job, gateway and channel that uses it.

| Dependency | Kind | Protocol | Time limit | Used by | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| eventBus | messageBroker | amqp | PT1S | channel loan.lifecycle, channel loan.overdue | The library's message broker, run by the library's IT team, which carries the loan events to the notification service and the audit log. |
| feeLedger | system | https | PT5S | operation returnLoan, operation reportLost | The finance system's ledger, where a late fee or a replacement charge is posted the moment it is charged. |

**Insight on eventBus:** A publish that the broker has not taken within a second is given up and retried, so a slow broker never holds a return at the desk.

**Insight on feeLedger:** The desk waits for the answer, so a call that takes longer than a few seconds is given up and the return is refused rather than left half done.

## 7. Endpoints

Every endpoint the system serves, with the permission a caller needs; public is open to everyone.

| Method | Path | Operation | Permission | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | /books | listBooks | public | Browse the catalogue |
| POST | /sessions | signIn | public | Sign in with an email address and a password |
| GET | /sessions/current | getSession | public | Who is signed in, and what they may do |
| GET | /profile | getProfile | signedIn | The member record of the person signed in |
| POST | /sessions/second-factor | confirmSecondFactor | public | Confirm a sign-in with the code of a second factor |
| POST | /password-resets | resetPassword | public | Set a new password with a reset code |
| GET | /members | listMembers | members.read | List members |
| POST | /members | createMember | members.write | Register a new member |
| GET | /members/{memberId} | getMember | members.read | One member with their loans |
| POST | /members/{memberId}/loans | lendCopies | loans.create | Lend several copies to a member at once |
| POST | /members/{memberId}/deactivate | deactivateMember | members.write | Deactivate a member, who then borrows nothing more |
| GET | /loans | listLoans | loans.read | List loans |
| POST | /loans | createLoan | loans.create | Lend a copy to a member |
| POST | /loans/{loanId}/return | returnLoan | loans.return | Record the return of a copy |
| POST | /loans/{loanId}/lost | reportLost | loans.return | Record a lost copy and charge its replacement cost |
| POST | /loans/{loanId}/fee-waivers | requestFeeWaiver | fees.request | Ask for a loan's late fee to be waived |
| GET | /fee-waivers | listFeeWaivers | fees.approve | List the requests to waive a late fee that wait for a desk supervisor |
| POST | /fee-waivers/{waiverId}/waive | waiveFee | fees.approve | Waive the late fee an approved request names |
| POST | /fee-waivers/{waiverId}/approve | approveFeeWaiver | fees.approve | Approve a request to waive a late fee, at its approve step |
| POST | /fee-waivers/{waiverId}/refuse | refuseFeeWaiver | fees.approve | Refuse a request to waive a late fee, at its approve step, saying why |

## 8. Settings

Every setting the system reads at run time. A secret's value is never written here; its description says where the value comes from.

| Setting | Type | Secret | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| dailyRate | decimal(10, 2) |  | The late fee per day, set by the board; read by the lateFee algorithm. |
| databaseUrl | string | yes | Where the database is; it carries the password, so it comes from the host's secret store and is never written here. |
| feeLedgerToken | string | yes | The token the finance team issued for the fee ledger; it comes from the host's secret store and is never written here. |
| notificationChannelUrl | string |  | Where the notification service listens for loan events. |

## 9. Backing up

The database is the only state; a nightly dump of it, kept for ninety days, is the backup.

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Dump the database | Every night after closing, dump the whole database to the backup store with the date in the file name. | The dump of the night is in the store and restores on a scratch server without error. |
| 2. Keep ninety days | Remove dumps older than ninety days. | The store holds ninety dumps, the newest from last night. |

## 10. Restoring

A restore puts one night's dump back in place of the live database; the loans since that night are re-entered from the desk's paper slips.

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Stop the service | Stop the service so that nothing writes while the database is replaced. | The desk screens show the service as down. |
| 2. Load the dump | Drop the live database and load the chosen night's dump into a new one of the same name. | The member and loan counts match the night's counts in the backup log. |
| 3. Start and check | Start the service and run the smoke check. | The catalogue answers and the loans list shows the restored loans. |

## 11. Rolling back

The previous build is kept installed beside the new one, so a rollback is a switch, and migrations are written to be reversible.

| Step | Action | Check |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Switch back | Point the service at the previous build and restart it. | The smoke check passes and the version shown is the previous one. |
| 2. Reverse the migrations | Run the rollback steps of every migration the release carried, newest first. | The schema gate against the previous entities passes. |
